question: Hypothyroidism is caused by which of the following anti-tubercular drug -
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Ethionamide" -> "inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis" -> "reduced thyroid hormone levels" -> "hypothyroidism" -> 85%
CHAIN: "PAS" -> "possible interference with thyroid function" -> "unclear impact on thyroid hormone levels" -> "possible hypothyroidism" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Cycloserine" -> "no known effect on thyroid function" -> "unlikely to cause hypothyroidism" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Pyrazinamide" -> "no known effect on thyroid function" -> "unlikely to cause hypothyroidism" -> 20%
analysis: Hypothyroidism can be caused by certain medications that interfere with thyroid hormone synthesis or function. Among the anti-tubercular drugs listed, ethionamide is known to inhibit thyroid hormone synthesis, which can lead to reduced thyroid hormone levels and result in hypothyroidism. This is a recognized side effect of ethionamide, making it the most likely candidate among the options provided. PAS (p-Aminosalicylic Acid) has been suggested to possibly interfere with thyroid function, but the evidence is not as strong or clear as it is for ethionamide. Cycloserine and pyrazinamide do not have known effects on thyroid function that would lead to hypothyroidism. Therefore, based on the available medical knowledge and consensus, ethionamide is the most likely anti-tubercular drug to cause hypothyroidism.
